skill.name: fit-scorer
skill.description: Scores shortlisted influencers against brand and campaign criteria, using weighted dimensions to recommend go, consider, or pass decisions.
skill.summary: Score and rank shortlisted influencers for campaign fit.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Static alerts were mostly caused by Markdown fences, inline paths, and repository documentation links. I confirmed one medium-risk issue: the skill shows a shell-style YouTube connector command using a candidate handle, which needs validation and non-shell execution guidance. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized network endpoint was found in the scanned files.

remediation.issue: Shell-style connector command accepts a candidate handle.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running the connector, validate handles against a strict allowlist, and pass arguments without a shell.

remediation.issue: Dynamic memory filenames are not explicitly constrained.
remediation.suggestion: State that topic and handle values must be slugified and kept under the documented memory directories.

remediation.issue: Relative documentation links trigger path traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that parent-directory links are documentation-only references, or replace them with marketplace-safe reference paths.

content.value_statement: Choosing creators by instinct wastes budget and hides brand-safety issues. This skill scores shortlisted influencers across weighted criteria and returns ranked go, consider, or pass recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Defines a weighted five-dimension influencer scoring framework.
Scores audience match, content quality, brand alignment, engagement quality, and partnership potential.
Applies ACE veto checks for follower fraud, brand safety, and bought engagement.
Produces a final 1-5 score with a clear campaign recommendation.
Compares multiple influencers in a ranked report with dimension-by-dimension notes.
Saves fit-score reports and promotes top picks for downstream skills.
limitations: It requires a user-provided shortlist and does not discover new influencers.
Score quality depends on the campaign brief and metric evidence provided.
Live platform measurements need optional connector access and user-approved credentials.
It does not contact creators or manage outreach workflows.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a creator shortlist
use_cases.description: Rank several candidate creators before outreach so budget goes to the strongest campaign fits.

use_cases.title: Defend partner selection
use_cases.description: Create a scored comparison that explains why one creator is preferred over similar alternatives.

use_cases.title: Standardize client recommendations
use_cases.description: Use the same scoring framework across client campaigns to make creator recommendations consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Score one influencer
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: evaluate a single creator against a simple campaign brief.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score @handle for our [brand] campaign. Goal: [awareness, engagement, or conversion]. Target audience: [audience]. Tell me whether to go, consider, or pass.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a shortlist
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: rank several creators using the default framework.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare @creator1, @creator2, and @creator3 for [campaign]. Rank them by fit, show each dimension score, and explain the best choice.

prompt_templates.title: Tune weights by goal
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: adjust weighting for a specific marketing objective.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score these creators for a conversion-focused campaign. Increase audience match and brand alignment weights, then explain how the ranking changes.

prompt_templates.title: Apply veto checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: include risk controls and evidence notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this shortlist with ACE veto checks for real followers, brand safety, and engagement authenticity. Cap any failed creator and cite the evidence.

output_examples.input: Score @sustainablesarah for a sustainable fashion conversion campaign.
output_examples.output: Final score: 4.4 out of 5. Verdict: Highly Recommended. The strongest factors are audience match and authentic engagement, with no veto failures found.

output_examples.input: Compare three creators for a skincare launch.
output: @creatorA ranks first because audience fit and disclosure history are strongest.
@creatorB is a Consider option due to good content but weaker engagement quality.
@creatorC is Pass because brand safety concerns cap the final rating.

output_examples.input: Use conversion weighting for a paid creator shortlist.
output_examples.output: The ranking favors creators with higher audience match and stronger partnership history. Content quality remains important but no longer drives the result alone.

best_practices: Provide the campaign goal, target audience, brand values, and available creator metrics.
Use the same evidence window for every creator in the shortlist.
Verify high-scoring creators before outreach, especially when authenticity signals are limited.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to find creators when no shortlist exists.
Do not change weights after seeing scores to force a preferred result.
Do not treat a score as proof when audience or engagement data is missing.

faq.question: Does this skill discover new influencers?
faq.answer: No. It scores and ranks a shortlist that the user already has.

faq.question: What dimensions does it score?
faq.answer: It scores audience match, content quality, brand alignment, engagement quality, and partnership potential.

faq.question: Can I change the weighting?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes weighting guidance for awareness, engagement, conversion, brand building, and long-term partnership goals.

faq.question: Does it require live social media access?
faq.answer: No. It can work from user-provided data, but optional connectors can improve measurement quality.

faq.question: How does it handle brand safety?
faq.answer: It includes brand safety scoring and ACE veto checks that can force a pass recommendation.

faq.question: Can it manage outreach after scoring?
faq.answer: No. It can hand off top-ranked creators, but outreach belongs in a separate workflow.
